plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A fast-growing subtropical tree with fern-like leaves that erupts in dense clusters of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers, often before the leaves fully emerge. Streets lined with jacarandas turn into purple corridors, and fallen blossoms carpet the ground beneath.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Southern Hemisphere (October to December)
plants.location: Native to South America; widely planted in Australia, South Africa (Pretoria), New Zealand's north, and Argentina
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City' because of its roughly 70,000 jacaranda trees, and University of Sydney students traditionally say that if a jacaranda flower falls on your head, you will pass your exams.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves that produces delicate, fragrant, often single or semi-double blooms in autumn when most other plants are winding down. It is valued as a hedge, espalier, or specimen and provides important late-season nectar for pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn to early winter (October to January) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to Japan; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Mediterranean Europe, and the UK
plants.funFact: Camellia sasanqua petals drop individually, unlike many Camellia japonica flowers, and its seeds are pressed to produce tea seed oil used in cooking and cosmetics in Asia.

plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub native to the tropical dry forests of Mexico whose showy 'flowers' are actually colorful modified leaves (bracts) surrounding tiny yellow true flowers called cyathia. In the wild it can grow into a tree several meters tall, with bracts coloring as days shorten.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; grown outdoors in warm climates and as a holiday potted plant worldwide
plants.funFact: Poinsettias are short-day plants that need about 12 hours of uninterrupted darkness nightly for roughly 8 to 10 weeks to develop their colorful bracts, and the Aztecs used the plant to produce a reddish dye.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A bold evergreen shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, up to 30 cm across, made up of pink-tipped bracts surrounding a central cone of tiny flowers. It thrives in the nutrient-poor, acidic soils of the fynbos and is adapted to periodic fire.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak bloom from about October to January
plants.location: Native to the fynbos of the Western and Eastern Cape, South Africa; cultivated in Australia, Hawaii, and California
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and the plant's thick underground lignotuber allows it to resprout after wildfires.
